backlog.spec: Pass a jac= argument to scipy minimize that returns the analytic gradient of the objective and the Jacobian of cons (pair distance terms, wall terms, and radius bounds) with respect to the 3n variables. Keep the constraint vector unchanged. This removes finite-difference evaluations, so each SLSQP iteration is much cheaper and more restarts fit into the 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: At the start of each restart, keep only the circle pairs whose centres are closer than a threshold (for example the sum of radii plus 0.3). Build the pair index list once from the initial centres and rebuild it after each SLSQP call. This shrinks the constraint vector from 325 pair terms to a few dozen, which speeds each SLSQP iteration. Re-check all pairs in the final repair step so validity is kept.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour constraints

backlog.spec: First minimise a penalty objective, minus the sum of radii plus a large weight times the squared positive parts of the overlap and wall violations, with L-BFGS-B on the 3n variables. Then hand the result to SLSQP with the exact constraints to polish. The penalty stage is cheap and gives SLSQP a better-conditioned start, so fewer SLSQP iterations are needed.
backlog.title: Two-stage penalty then SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP call with an augmented Lagrangian loop. Use L-BFGS-B with simple bounds on the centres and radii to minimise the Lagrangian for the pair and wall constraints, then update the multipliers and the penalty weight, and repeat for about 8 outer rounds. Finish with one short SLSQP polish. This keeps each inner solve well conditioned.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian outer loop

backlog.spec: After the first random restart, repeatedly perturb the best packing found so far. Pick one to three circles at random, move them to random positions, and re-run SLSQP from the perturbed state. Accept the new packing only if its repaired radius sum is higher. Keep the random restarts as a fallback for a fraction of the budget, for example 20 percent.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Given a good packing, remove the circle with the smallest radius. Find the largest empty spot by evaluating a dense grid of candidate points and taking the one with the greatest distance to all other circles and the walls. Place the removed circle there, then run SLSQP. Accept if the sum of radii improves. Repeat until the time budget is used.
backlog.title: Remove smallest circle and reinsert into largest hole

backlog.spec: From a good packing, pick two circles with clearly different radii and swap their centres while keeping the radii attached to the positions. Run SLSQP from the swapped state and keep the result only if the repaired sum improves. This explores assignments of big and small circles to positions without changing the number of circles.
backlog.title: Swap moves between radius classes

backlog.spec: Maintain a pool of the best eight packings found so far, sorted by repaired radius sum. For each new trial, pick two pool members, take the centres of the first on one side of a random line and of the second on the other side, fill any mismatch by moving the nearest circles, and run SLSQP from that child. Insert the child into the pool if it beats the worst member and is not a duplicate.
backlog.title: Elite pool with recombination

backlog.spec: Run many restarts with a small MAX_ITER, for example 60, and record each repaired sum. Take the best five from those and run each one with a large MAX_ITER and a tight tolerance. Return the best polished result. This spends most of the budget on exploration and the remainder on exact convergence of the most promising starts.
backlog.title: Cheap short runs then polish the top few

backlog.spec: Track the best repaired sum seen so far. If the last K restarts (K around 10) have not improved it, stop spending time on pure random starts and switch to perturbation of the incumbent for the rest of the budget. Otherwise continue random restarts. This redirects time to the search mode that is currently producing gains.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart allocation

backlog.spec: Change TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 and estimate the duration of the last restart. Start a new restart only if the elapsed time plus that estimate stays under 0.9 times the limit, so the call never exceeds 45 s. This gives about 12 percent more search time at no code complexity cost.
backlog.title: Raise the time fraction and guard the deadline

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 500 and set SLSQP options ftol to 1e-12 so that the solver converges on each start instead of stopping early. Check the time per restart stays acceptable, since fewer restarts will fit in the budget. Rely on the repair step to fix the small residual overlaps.
backlog.title: Increase SLSQP iteration cap with tight tolerance

backlog.spec: Start each restart with all radii scaled to a small fraction of the feasible size, then run SLSQP in several stages where a scale factor on the radius bounds grows from 0.5 to 1.0. Each stage starts from the previous stage's centres. This lets circles spread out before they are pushed to their maximal radii, which reduces jams.
backlog.title: Progressive radius growth schedule

backlog.spec: When perturbing the incumbent, add Gaussian noise to all centres with standard deviation that starts at 0.05 and decays geometrically to 0.002 over the remaining budget. Re-run SLSQP after each jitter and accept only improvements. Large early jitter explores wide, small late jitter refines the current basin.
backlog.title: Decaying jitter for basin hopping

backlog.spec: Keep a current packing and a temperature. Each new local optimum is accepted if its repaired sum is higher, or with probability exp(delta over temperature) if it is lower. Lower the temperature geometrically over the run. Always store the best packing seen separately and return it, not the current state.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing acceptance over restarts

backlog.spec: Instead of setting every initial radius to INIT_RADIUS, draw initial radii uniformly from 0.02 to 0.12 using the seeded rng. Unequal starting sizes break the symmetry that causes many restarts to converge to the same equal-circle arrangement. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Random radii initialisation

backlog.spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.0 so initial centres are drawn over the whole square rather than an inner box, which places circles nearer the walls from the start. Combine this with clipping so no centre is outside the square before SLSQP. Walls then become active earlier in the optimisation, which can lead to different basins.
backlog.title: Full-square uniform start

backlog.spec: Generate initial centres by farthest-point sampling: draw a few hundred random candidates with the seeded rng, then pick each next centre as the candidate farthest from all already chosen centres, starting from a random one. This gives well-spread starts with fewer near-coincident pairs, so SLSQP begins from a more feasible configuration.
backlog.title: Farthest-point sampling initialisation

backlog.spec: Generate a hexagonal lattice of points slightly denser than 26 points inside the square, with random orientation and offset drawn from the seeded rng. Randomly delete points until exactly n remain. Use these as initial centres with radii set to the nearest-neighbour half distance. This biases starts toward dense local packings.
backlog.title: Hexagonal lattice starts with random removal

backlog.spec: For a random restart, generate half the centres at random and mirror them across a randomly chosen axis of symmetry of the square (the vertical or horizontal midline, or the diagonal), filling the rest so the count is exactly n. Run SLSQP with symmetry not enforced, so it can break symmetry later. Many best known packings have such structure, so these starts land in good basins more often.
backlog.title: Symmetric initialisation

backlog.spec: Initialise each radius to half the distance from its centre to its nearest other centre, capped at the distance to the nearest wall times two, then multiply by 0.9 to make the start feasible. This gives SLSQP a nearly feasible starting point rather than a set of overlapping circles of fixed size.
backlog.title: Nearest-neighbour radius initialisation

backlog.spec: Draw a fraction, about 40 percent, of the initial centres uniformly on the boundary band of width 0.15 near the four walls, and the remainder uniformly in the interior. Good packings of this kind put many small circles along the edges, so biasing starts toward edges can improve the sum of radii.
backlog.title: Edge-biased centre sampling

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a few hundred steps of gradient descent on an energy that adds a soft repulsion between all pairs, inversely proportional to squared distance, and a soft wall repulsion, while the radii are held fixed at the starting values. This spreads centres apart and removes near-coincident pairs. Then run SLSQP as usual.
backlog.title: Penalty repulsion warm-up regularisation

backlog.spec: Add a small quadratic penalty on the deviation of each radius from the mean radius of the current packing, with coefficient about 1e-3, to the SLSQP objective during the first half of the iterations, then remove it. This discourages extreme radius distributions early, which helps SLSQP pass through better basins before final optimisation of the true sum.
backlog.title: Radius-sum regularised objective

backlog.spec: Let the SLSQP constraints allow a tiny overlap of 1e-7. Then instead of the global shrink loop in _repair, scale each radius pair involved in an overlap by the exact ratio only for that pair, process pairs in decreasing overlap order, and recheck walls after each step. This loses less radius than the current repair while still giving a valid packing within 1e-10.
backlog.title: Overlap slack with exact greedy repair

backlog.spec: After a packing is validated, visit circles in random order and increase each radius to the maximum value allowed by the current neighbours and walls, using the exact distance constraints. Repeat the sweep twice. This recovers slack that the shrink repair leaves behind, with no change to the centres.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth after optimisation

backlog.spec: Solve the problem for n minus one circles first using the same search, then add one circle at the largest hole found on a grid, and run SLSQP on all n circles from that start. Use this incremental starting point as one of the restart seeds in the mix. Good packings for consecutive n often share structure, so this supplies a different family of starts.
backlog.title: Incremental construction from n minus one

backlog.spec: Alternate each restart between two solver configurations: SLSQP directly from random starts, and a two-stage penalty then SLSQP pipeline. Keep statistics of which configuration produced each new best repaired sum, and in the second half of the budget allocate restarts in proportion to their success rate. This uses whichever start procedure works best on the instance.
backlog.title: Multi-start with a bounded number of SLSQP variants
